title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Ligand substituents and assembly can redirect antenna energy flow: an intermediate charge-transfer state can sustain efficient Eu3+ sensitization even when the S1–T1 gap is outside the usual optimum, while aggregation or mechanical confinement shortens the donor–acceptor path.
explanation: Substituent-tuned S1, T1, and CT energies are cited as enabling transfer despite a non-ideal singlet–triplet gap. AIE ligands in lanthanide organic cages increase ligand-to-Eu3+ transfer and upconversion brightness. A compact [2]rotaxane uses the mechanical bond to confine antenna and emitter and favor Dexter transfer.
scope: Antenna-sensitized lanthanide luminescence, especially Eu3+ complexes, cages, and mechanically interlocked emitters.
conditions: Substituent control of CT states; aggregation of AIE ligands; short antenna–metal distances enforced by a mechanical bond.
caveats: The review does not specify numerical energy gaps or transfer rates for these 2025 cases.
